findings.text: queue_pane_row renders the four-part waiting row and the no-work-running fault, but no production code calls it: git grep over the head tree finds only tests/test_the_queue_view_counts_waits_by_cause.py, and the live pane's waiting count is produced by reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:2388, so no reader ever sees the split or the fault the plan requires.
RUNNING_PHASES re-declares the in-flight phase set that reckon/crew/ticker.py:3263 already owns as IN_FLIGHT_PHASES; the two now drift independently if a phase is added.

wait_part_of returns SLOT for every phase that is not awaiting-upstream, so a request in the held phase (a paused gate) is counted as waiting for a lane slot, which is the opposite of what a reader diagnosing '14 waiting, nothing running' needs to know.

counts.waiting is a second key holding exactly len(requests), the value counts.requests already publishes, so two names now claim the same figure and a future filter applied to one will silently disagree with the other.

WAIT_PART_LETTERS restates the four part names that reckon/crew/queue_view.py:48 QUEUE_WAIT_PARTS owns, rather than importing them, so a renamed part would leave the renderer keying on a name the view no longer emits.
